items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy 'what if' geography Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't believe how cool this story is and can't wait to tell you. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright and punchy, loud-ish and lively. Wide, dramatic pitch movement: rise with real wonder on every question, hit every number with genuine amazement ('WOW' energy), build excitement through each line, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. 'Plot twist' gets a playful, knowing, excited lift. 'But that's not even the weirdest part' is whispered-excited, leaning in like a secret. The three capitals 'Tallinn? Riga? Vilnius?' are asked like a quick, rising, playful quiz. 'It's closer to Finnish.' is deadpan and funny. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because honestly...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 175 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy, bored or documentary-serious. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy level throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Say GTA as the letters G-T-A. Pronounce 'Tallinn' as 'TAL-in', 'Riga' as 'REE-gah', 'Vilnius' as 'VIL-nee-us', 'Lithuania' as 'lith-oo-AY-nee-ah'. Read ONLY the text provided, word for word, every line in order; never add words of your own.
lines: What if Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania... became one country?
Plot twist: for one day, they already acted like one.
In nineteen eighty-nine, two million people held hands...
in one unbroken chain... six hundred seventy-five kilometers long.
From Tallinn... through Riga... to Vilnius.
So what would this country get?
and land about the size of Florida.
But here's the catch: they can't understand each other.
Then there's the capital. Tallinn? Riga? Vilnius?
But that's not even the weirdest part.
About six hundred years ago, Lithuania alone...
was the biggest country in Europe.
It reached from the Baltic Sea... to the Black Sea.
And today? All three joined the E-U on the very same day.
And Latvia has just one thing to say.
So... one country, or three? Because honestly...
